messages.text: Ombudsman all set for Japan Cup swansong

metadata.summary: Having already cemented his status as a Godolphin great, Ombudsman will have the chance to end his stellar career on the global stage when tackling the Japan Cup later this month.
metadata.content: Ombudsman: Godolphin great set for Japan Cup swansong | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Ombudsman: Godolphin great set for Japan Cup swansong Champion Stakes hero Ombudsman is set for one final start in the Japan Cup before being retired to stud, trainer John Gosden has confirmed; The Godolphin-owned star, who is the back-to-back winner of the Prince Of Wales's Stakes, missed out on a trip to the Breeders' Cup last month. Tuesday 10 November 2026 14:01, UK Image: Ombudsman is set for a final start in the Japan Cup Having already cemented his status as a Godolphin great, Ombudsman will have the chance to end his stellar career on the global stage when tackling the Japan Cup later this month. Joint-trainers John and Thady Gosden elected against a Breeders' Cup run for the son of Night Of Thunder after his victory in the Champion Stakes, but he will now tackle a mile and a half for the first time in Tokyo on November 29 before stallion duties await at Darley's Kildangan Stud in Ireland in 2027. However, win, lose or draw in the Far East, Godolphin's managing director Hugh Anderson believes his legacy has already been secured and he will go down as "one of the best" to represent Sheikh Mohammed's operation on the racetrack. He told the Press Association: "John is a master trainer and has obviously got his eye very firmly on this prize. It's very exciting. messages.text: England Wheelchair rout Australia to reach World Cup final

metadata.summary: England Wheelchair scored a record points total against rival Australia to rout their opponents 86-18 and reach their fifth successive Rugby League World Cup final.

The game was all but over at half-time as England held a 40-6 lead, with Rob Hawkins leading the charge for his side with a stunning 30-point performance in his side's dominant victory. The win means the defending World Cup champions will face France in the final in Wollongong on Friday, with a chance to claim their third World Cup title. The prospect of a trilogy fight with Tyson Fury could tempt Oleksandr Usyk to call off his move out of the heavyweight division, says promoter Frank Warren. Usyk has an outstanding legacy at heavyweight, having previously beaten Fury twice and twice become the undisputed champion of the division without losing a fight. But he has previously also been an undisputed champion at cruiserweight and his team have revealed that he could return to his old weight class , where star names like David Benavidez and Jai Opetaia could become targets. messages.text: Tough-tackling Schlager proves his worth for Forest

metadata.summary: Xaver Schlager has been quietly impressive for Nottingham Forest this season but what was missing was that big moment. It came in the 3-1 win over Manchester City on Saturday when he dispossessed Elliot Anderson for Liam Delap's first goal.

Adam Bate Football Features Writer @ghostgoal Tuesday 10 November 2026 10:49, UK Image: Xaver Schlager is an underrated player but he enjoyed a big moment in Nottingham Forest's win over Manchester City Xaver Schlager has been quietly impressive for Nottingham Forest this season but what was missing was that big moment. It came in the 3-1 win over Manchester City on Saturday when he dispossessed Elliot Anderson for Liam Delap's first goal. The free transfer from Leipzig nipped in ahead of the £116m man that he has replaced in Forest's midfield and set Delap on the way to doubling the lead. Schlager is no Anderson but he has his own qualities and they made the difference at the weekend. "It was a top team performance and it was a top performance by Xaver Schlager," said Forest boss Oliver Glasner in the press conference afterwards. messages.text: Lure of the Championship - Why foreign coaches are drawn to England's second tier

metadata.summary: The focus is often on the lack of opportunities for British coaches but look at it another way and it is remarkable that 16 of the clubs in the sixth-richest league in European football – two thirds of them – are currently being coached by men from the British Isles.
